title: Post draft-atwood-jmap-updates-00 to datatracker (IETF 127 week)
description:
Post draft-atwood-jmap-updates-00 to the IETF datatracker before the jmap@ email (jmap-chat-spec-0577) goes out. Target Sunday 2026-11-15, IETF 127 week (moved from Monday, Mark 2026-11-15). The submission tool reopens after 2026-11-14 23:59 PST, i.e. 2026-11-15 08:00 UTC (notice on https://datatracker.ietf.org/submit/, checked 2026-11-15 04:04 UTC). Before that, the API returns an error. Posting is public and outward-facing, so it needs Mark's explicit go-ahead for this specific submission.

Note: this is the first draft in the corpus with category std and submissiontype IETF; the others are exp and independent. That fits a document that updates RFC 8620 and RFC 9425.

Datatracker login (the API 'user' field): mark@reviewcommit.com (Mark, 2026-11-15).

Procedure (datatracker submission API, per https://datatracker.ietf.org/api/submission, checked 2026-11-15; no API key, XML-only uploads, multipart/form-data so use curl, not wget):

1. Build and check, from /data/PROJECT/jmap-chat-spec (S = session scratchpad; X = $S/v3, an empty dir):
     kramdown-rfc draft-atwood-jmap-updates-00.md > $S/kd.xml
     mkdir -p $X && xml2rfc -q --v2v3 $S/kd.xml -o $X/draft-atwood-jmap-updates-00.xml   # kramdown-rfc 1.7.43 emits v2 vocabulary even with -3; submit the converted v3 file
     xml2rfc -q --text $X/draft-atwood-jmap-updates-00.xml -o $X/draft-atwood-jmap-updates-00.txt   # expect no warnings
     /data/ietf-tools/node/bin/idnits $X/draft-atwood-jmap-updates-00.xml
     /data/ietf-tools/node/bin/idnits $X/draft-atwood-jmap-updates-00.txt
   Expected result (checked 2026-11-15): 0 errors. Known, accepted nits: RFC 7807 obsolete-reference warning (cited on purpose, describing 8620's old reference); "already updated by RFC9404, RFC9670" warning (no conflict: those add capabilities, this adds guidance); cross-stream comments (false positive, submissiontype IETF); UAX29 external normative ref (stable Unicode annex); BCP14 keywords not in <bcp14> tags; <?line?> PIs; RFC link format (renderer). The filename must equal the draft name or idnits errors. Fix anything new; commit and push the fix first, so the posted -00 matches the repo.

2. Submit (after go-ahead):
     curl -s -F "user=mark@reviewcommit.com" -F "xml=@$X/draft-atwood-jmap-updates-00.xml" https://datatracker.ietf.org/api/submission
   Success: JSON {id, name, rev, status_url}. Failure: {"error": "..."}. If the error says submissions are closed, the post-meeting-cutoff window has not reopened yet; stop and tell Mark.

3. Poll status (every minute or so; don't hammer it):
     curl -s https://datatracker.ietf.org/api/submission/<id>/status
   'validating' = still processing. 'auth' = passed, waiting for email confirmation. 'cancel' = failed or cancelled; read https://datatracker.ietf.org/submit/status/<id>/ for why.

4. Email confirmation (Mark clicks; the API cannot skip it). At 'auth' the datatracker emails a confirmation link, expected at the author address in the draft (mark@reviewcommit.com). Find it with fm (search for the draft name from the datatracker) and give Mark the link. He opens it and confirms.

5. Verify https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/draft-atwood-jmap-updates/ resolves and shows -00. Update 0577 if the URL differs. Then close this bead, which unblocks 0577.
